text: A plumbing plan can't name a file the repository's ignore rules match, and a build's commit holds every file the build wrote (#840). git leaves an ignored file out of a commit without a word: #802's ratified plan named internal/verify/coverage.go under a coverage.* rule, the build wrote and tested it, and the published branch lacked it and didn't compile. The plan check now asks git which of a plan's files, acceptance tests and its own record the rules match, and refuses the plan with the file and the rule, before any test runs. When a build or a ratification is committed, each file it wrote is added by name, rules or no rules, so the branch is what was built and tested. A file the repository already tracks is never ignored, and what a build didn't write stays ignored.
